thread.title: Murder suspect arrested in San Bernardino County after nearly 2 years on the run - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Murder suspect arrested in San Bernardino County after nearly 2 years on the run - NewsBreak

author: Vivian Chow
title: Murder suspect arrested in San Bernardino County after nearly 2 years on the run - NewsBreak
text:
By Vivian Chow No media credit provided. ,
2 hours ago
A 26-year-old man wanted for murder in Oregon was arrested in Southern California after he fled the state and spent nearly two years on the run.
The San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department identified the suspect as Rodney Rogers, 26. Deputies said the man is believed to be a transient.
Rogers was wanted in connection with a homicide in late 2024 after Portland police officers in Oregon found a victim who had been fatally shot.
Authorities issued an arrest warrant for murder after identifying Rogers as the suspect.
Following an investigation, detectives believed Rogers had fled the state and was staying in the San Bernardino County area.
On July 2, 2026, investigators received additional information indicating he was in the Loma Linda area, SBSD said.
“Acting on that information and employing a variety of investigative techniques, investigators located Rogers at a business plaza in the 25000 block of Barton Road,” authorities said.
He was taken into custody and transported to the Central Detention Center, where he was booked pending extradition to Oregon.
No further details, including the victim’s identity or a possible motive for the murder, were released as the case remains under investigation.
